subject.title: Support Slack user-level events (events on behalf of users) for DM routing

question: Should the Slack plugin support acting as a configured Slack user account for inbound DMs, and what explicit opt-in/token-scope boundary should gate it?
rationale: This changes OpenClaw from bot/app identity into human-user identity for inbound routing and replies, which affects workspace trust, tool authority, and token-scope exposure.

options.title: Add explicit user-agent mode
options.body: Implement a clearly named Slack plugin mode that validates user scopes, routes on Slack event authorizations, and uses the matching user token only for that opted-in identity path.

options.title: Keep bot identity only
options.body: Document that Slack user tokens are for reads and limited fallback behavior, while inbound DMs and normal replies stay bot/app identity only.

options.title: Prototype outside the bundled plugin
options.body: Require this behavior to prove out in an external Slack plugin or ClawHub package before adopting it as an official bundled capability.

recommendation.title: Add explicit user-agent mode
recommendation.body: Implement a clearly named Slack plugin mode that validates user scopes, routes on Slack event authorizations, and uses the matching user token only for that opted-in identity path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main ownership of the Slack plugin monitor/account code makes this the best available routing candidate for the security/product boundary decision.
